title: Riverbend Library SMS hold-ready notices
context: Riverbend Public Library is a city library system (9 branches, about 180,000 active cardholders) running self-hosted Koha, the open-source library system. The state's library-records confidentiality statute forbids disclosing which materials a patron has borrowed or requested. This plan adds text-message notices for holds ready for pickup. Agreed constraints: no patron may lose hold notices because of this change; opt-in only; stay within the approved notices budget. It is about to be handed to the library systems developer for a 4-week build.
artifact:
# Plan: SMS hold-ready notices

Team: library systems developer (1), circulation lead (0.5) · 4 weeks · Ticket LIBSYS-318

## 1. Why
- Hold-ready notices today: email 71%, automated phone call 29% (~41,000 calls/month via CallNotify at $0.11/call ≈ $4,500/month). The CallNotify contract ends 2027-03-31 and will not be renewed (board decision, Sep 2026).
- 18% of calls reach voicemail or no answer. Uncollected-hold expiry rate: 9.2% for phone-notice patrons vs 5.1% for email (Koha reports, Jan–Sep 2026).
- 2026 patron survey (n = 2,340): 64% of phone-notice patrons would prefer a text message.

## 2. Scope
- In: an SMS option for the "Hold filled" notice only, using Koha's built-in SMS transport.
- Out: due-date, overdue and fines notices (later phase, separate plan); two-way messaging; what replaces calls for patrons who stay on phone after March 2027 (LIBSYS-330).

## 3. How it works
- Koha sends SMS through its `SMSSendDriver` system preference (SMS::Send driver interface), configured for the provider selected in RFP LIBSYS-301 (contract signed Oct 2). Switching providers later is a config change, not a code change.
- Patron messaging preferences already support an SMS transport per notice type; we enable it for "Hold filled" only.
- Template (English, plus Spanish for patrons whose preferred language is Spanish, via `TranslateNotices`), GSM-7, one segment:
  "Riverbend Library: 1 item is ready for pickup at Eastside Branch until Nov 4. Reply STOP to opt out, HELP for help."
  - No patron name, title, author or barcode. A reassigned number or shared phone reveals nothing about what the patron requested.
  - Count, branch and date come from notice template variables; the per-item title loop used in the email template is deliberately left out.
- HELP auto-reply (configured at the provider): "Riverbend Library hold notices. Call 555-0142 or visit riverbendlibrary.org/sms. Reply STOP to cancel."
- Quiet hours: `process_message_queue.pl --type sms` runs every 15 minutes between 09:00 and 20:00 local only, so a hold filled after 20:00 is texted at 09:00. Pickup windows are 7 days; the delay costs at most 13 hours.

## 4. Consent and opt-out
- Opt-in only. Patrons choose SMS in the OPAC under "Your messaging", or staff set it at the desk when the patron asks and provides a mobile number. Patron attribute `SMS_CONSENT` records the date and source (opac/desk).
- Existing phone numbers are not auto-enrolled. Nobody gets a text they did not ask for.
- On enrolment, Koha sends one confirmation text: "Riverbend Library: you'll get a text when holds are ready for pickup. Msg frequency varies. Msg & data rates may apply. Reply STOP to cancel, HELP for help." The patron's previous hold-notice channel is saved in patron attribute `NOTICE_PREV` (new sign-ups who pick SMS get `phone`; every SMS patron has a mobile number).
- STOP: the provider handles carrier-required keyword replies and blocks further sends to that number. A webhook receiver (~150 lines, on the existing Koha app server behind the existing nginx/TLS) exposes a single rate-limited POST path, verifies the provider's request signature, then:
  - switches every patron whose SMS number matches (family members can share a phone) from SMS back to their own `NOTICE_PREV`, so they keep getting notices;
  - adds a circulation note visible to staff.
- The receiver uses a dedicated DB user with UPDATE only on `borrower_message_transport_preferences` and `borrower_attributes`, and INSERT only on `message_queue` and `messages`.
- Delivery failures: on an `undelivered`/`failed` status callback, the receiver queues the same notice on the patron's `NOTICE_PREV` channel. After 2 consecutive failures it switches the patron back to `NOTICE_PREV` and adds a staff note to verify the number.
- 10DLC: brand registration approved Oct 14. The "Library account notifications" campaign was submitted Oct 20; typical approval is 1–3 weeks. Public launch is gated on approval.

## 5. Privacy and data handling
- The provider receives only the phone number and the message body above. The contract includes a DPA and a library-records confidentiality clause reviewed by the city attorney (Oct 1). Message bodies are redacted at the provider after delivery; delivery metadata is kept 90 days per contract.
- Koha `message_queue` rows are purged after 30 days by the existing `cleanup_database.pl` job (unchanged).
- Webhook receiver logs status, Koha message id and timestamp only; never message bodies; phone numbers as the last 4 digits.

## 6. Cost
- ~141,000 hold notices/month (100k email, 41k phone).
- Assumed uptake: 50% of phone patrons + 10% of email patrons ≈ 30,500 texts/month.
- ~$0.011 per text including carrier fees → ~$335/month, plus ~$19/month for number and campaign fees.
- Calls drop by ~20,500/month → ~$2,250/month saved while CallNotify runs.
- Approved notices budget allows up to $600/month for SMS (finance memo FIN-2026-117); a provider spend alert fires at $450.

## 7. Rollout
- Weeks 1–2: driver config, en/es templates, webhook receiver, rollback script, desk procedure and a 1-page staff guide.
- Week 3: staff pilot. 40 staff cardholders opt in; we verify delivery, quiet hours, STOP, HELP and the failure fallback (one deliberately invalid number).
- Week 4, after 10DLC approval: OPAC option enabled systemwide, branch signage, and a line in the email newsletter. No bulk texting.

## 8. Rollback
- `sms_rollback.pl`, written and tested in week 2 against a staging copy of the patron database:
  1. For every patron with SMS on "Hold filled", restore `NOTICE_PREV` (email or phone call; print notice once CallNotify has ended).
  2. Re-queue any pending SMS rows in `message_queue` on the restored channel, so holds filled around the rollback still get a notice.
  3. Clear `SMSSendDriver`.
- Consent and opt-out records are kept, so re-enabling later never texts anyone who sent STOP.
- Patrons who enrolled after launch end up on exactly the channel they had before.

## 9. Measures (90 days after launch)
- Delivery rate ≥ 97% (provider status callbacks).
- Uncollected-hold expiry rate for SMS patrons ≤ 5.5% (phone today: 9.2%).
- STOP and fallback counts reported monthly to the circulation team.
decoys: Sending hold notices through a third-party SMS provider could disclose patrons' requested materials. The message contains no name, title, author or barcode (the title loop is deliberately omitted), the provider has a DPA and confidentiality clause, bodies are redacted after delivery, and receiver logs omit bodies and full numbers.

Texting patrons raises consent and opt-out obligations. The plan is opt-in only with recorded consent, never auto-enrols existing phone numbers, sends a compliant confirmation text, honours STOP/HELP at the provider and in Koha (falling back to the patron's previous channel so no notices are lost), observes quiet hours, and gates launch on 10DLC approval.
